edit.goal.description.md:
Shrink the supply-chain surface: fewer third-party packages reach users and dev machines, and the ones left are deliberate.

Done when `npm i epiq` installs no third-party packages, and every remaining dependency is either core (react, ink, zod, shiki…) or too risky to own (ws, markdown).

Measure with `node source/scripts/dep-stats.mjs`. Before (main 0d6d79a, 2026-11-20):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `npm i epiq`: direct deps | 15 | |
| `npm i epiq`: packages installed | 258 | |
| dev: direct deps | 40 | |
| dev: packages installed | 611 | |
| dev: packages with install scripts | 3 (esbuild, fsevents, node-pty) | |

Largest shipped trees: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 93, react-markdown 82, remark-gfm 68, @pierre/diffs 50, ink 38, remark-breaks 17.

add.issue.name: npm package bundles its dependencies, so `npm i epiq` installs none

edit.description.md:
`build:npm` uses `--packages=external`, so npm users install 258 packages on their own, resolved from version ranges at install time. GUI-only packages (react-markdown, remark-*, @pierre/diffs, react-router-dom, react-dom) are already bundled into dist/gui, but they're still listed under `dependencies`.

- Bundle the Node entries the way the SEA build already does (require shim, devtools stub, NODE_ENV).
- Move every runtime package to `devDependencies`. Users then get the exact versions we locked and tested.
- Fix along the way: `chalk` is a devDependency used at runtime (it only works because ink hoists it); `@xterm/headless` is test-only but listed as runtime.

add.issue.name: CLI parses its flags with node:util parseArgs, not meow

edit.description.md: meow is one call in `source/Index.tsx`. Node's built-in `parseArgs` covers it; the help text is ours already.

add.issue.name: MCP server speaks stdio JSON-RPC itself, without @modelcontextprotocol/sdk

edit.description.md:
The SDK is the largest shipped tree (93 packages: express, hono, cors, jose, ajv, cross-spawn, eventsource…) for HTTP/OAuth transports we never use. We use `McpServer` + `StdioServerTransport`; tests use `Client` + `InMemoryTransport`.

A stdio server is ~300–400 lines: initialize (version negotiation), tools/list, tools/call, ping, notifications. zod 4's `z.toJSONSchema` replaces ajv/zod-to-json-schema. Risk: tracking spec changes. Keep a test against the real SDK client so we notice when the protocol drifts.

add.issue.name: Event ids come from our own ULID module, not the ulid package

edit.description.md: We use `ulid`, `monotonicFactory`, `decodeTime` and `encodeTime` across 43 files. That's ~60 lines on `crypto.getRandomValues`, and these ids order the whole event log, so the code is worth owning. Needs a test comparing it against the package (encoding, monotonic increments, decode) before the swap.

4 files use `createBrowserRouter`, `RouterProvider`, `Navigate`, `useSearchParams` and `useNavigationType`. Replace with a small history/search-param hook, keeping the rule that only back/forward navigation (POP) re-reads URL state. It's bundled into the GUI, so this only reduces build-time exposure.

add.issue.name: Dev installs run no third-party install scripts and skip brand-new versions

edit.description.md:
Install scripts are how the recent npm worms spread. Today 3 packages have them: esbuild, fsevents and node-pty.

Options:
1. `ignore-scripts=true` in `.npmrc`, then explicitly rebuild esbuild and node-pty, and run husky's `prepare` ourselves. Safest, but every install becomes a two-step chore and the hooks can silently go missing.
2. Keep scripts, but add a Dependabot/Renovate cooldown so a version has to be days old before we adopt it. Cheap; catches most worms, which are usually pulled within hours.

Recommend 2 now, and 1 if the dev tree stays large.

eslint-plugin-react pulls in 124 packages, the largest dev tree. Check which of its rules we actually rely on: drop it if hooks + TypeScript cover them, or replace the few that matter with local rules in `eslint-rules.mjs`.

Solution: `source/lib/event/ulid.ts` (~85 lines, no imports) replaces the package in 72 files; the package is removed. It keeps the package's contract, including throwing on an undecodable id, which callers already catch, so there's no behavior change.

add.issue.comment.md:
Re-verified against ulid 3.0.2: 553k cases, 0 mismatches. Covers random and hostile ids (lower case, I/L/O/U, ß, ligatures, emoji, NUL, wrong lengths), encodeTime edges, and monotonic sequences including now/NaN/negative seeds and their throw points.

Review flagged that `ß` uppercases to `SS` and so decodes. Deliberately kept: changing what decodes would make old and new clients disagree about a hostile id's time.

edit.goal.description.md:
MCP replies and tool definitions carry only what an agent reads, so a session spends its context on work, not on board plumbing.

Done when no read can return an unbounded reply, routine list replies are ~30% smaller or more, and tool definitions are trimmed.

Measured on a clone of this board (60 open issues, 8.4k events), chars/3.6 ≈ tokens:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| tool definitions (52 tools) | ~6.5k | |
| `epiq_state_get` | ~1,368k | |
| `epiq_issue_list` (brief) | ~4.1k | |
| `epiq_issue_list` (brief: false) | ~23.9k | |
| `epiq_contributor_list` | ~1.4k | |
| `epiq_board_list` | ~1.2k | |
| `epiq_goal_list` | ~1.2k | |
| `epiq_issue_get` | ~0.55k | |

Follows the closed goal "Lean MCP".

add.issue.name: epiq_state_get returns ~1.4M tokens on this board: the whole event log and every raw node

edit.description.md:
On a clone of our board it returns 4.9 MB: `eventLog` with 8,437 events (~967k tokens) and `nodes` (~401k). A single call by an agent fills or overflows its context, and it grows with the board's age.

Options:
1. **Remove it.** issue_list/get, board_list, goal_list and swimlane_list already cover reads. Simplest; any agent prompt that names the tool breaks.
2. **Make it a bounded overview** (boards → lanes → issue counts, no log), with the log behind explicit `since`/`limit` params. Keeps the name; one more read to maintain.

Recommend 2, with a hard cap on the log page.

add.issue.name: Replies carry only what an agent reads: no colours, default flags, empty arrays or float noise

edit.description.md:
Every row repeats fields an agent never uses:
- hex colours on assignees, goals and contributors
- `false` flags (isSelf, isExternal, isRemoved, readonly, isClosed, countsDone, doneByName)
- empty `tags: []` and `assignees: []`
- a full goal object on each issue
- 16-digit floats in stats (`concentration: 0.7541111981205951`)

Trimming these (omit defaults and empties, goal by name, round floats) on today's replies:
- `epiq_issue_list`: 4.1k → 2.9k tokens (−30%); 2.7k if grouped by lane
- `epiq_contributor_list`: 1.4k → 0.4k (−70%)

Also: writes into a lane echo its whole `laneDescription` on every call, and `epiq_board_list` embeds every goal's member list, duplicating `epiq_goal_list`.

Reply shapes are read by agents, not stored, so this changes no event or log format. The GUI has its own API, so it's unaffected.

add.issue.name: Tool definitions cost ~6.5k tokens: trim descriptions and schemas

edit.description.md:
52 tools: ~2.3k tokens of descriptions, ~2.6k of input schemas. Clients without deferred tool loading pay all of it on every session.
- `repoRoot` is declared on all 52 tools.
- issue_move and swimlane_move spell `position` as four oneOf variants (~200 tokens each); `{at: start|end|before|after, sibling?}` says the same.
- The longest descriptions run to 100–230 tokens: repo_connect, project_init, actor_assume, contributor_email_link.
Target: −30% without dropping anything an agent needs to call a tool correctly.

add.issue.comment.md: Before the performance work (bcb1db9~1) this reply was ~10M tokens on the same clone. #609 cut it 7×, since nodes stopped carrying copies of their events. Every other read is byte-for-byte the same size before and after #606–#610.
add.issue.comment.author: JRDKBJCGCAZ8DVAH0BHTBQYV1B
